title: Ring map quasi-finite at a prime (affine notion)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of finite type ($S$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra), let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring, $j:S\to F$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$, and let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\subset F$ be the prime ideal of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$, i.e. the unique prime ideal of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$ (it exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]). We say that $R\to S$ is *quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$* if $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that is, the singleton $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. (Stacks Project, Algebra, Definition 10.122.3 (1), Tag 00PL (definition-quasi-finite), which takes any of the equivalent conditions of Algebra, Lemma 10.122.2, Tag 00PK (lemma-isolated-point-fibre); this is condition (1) of 00PK. A ring map $R\to S$ is *quasi-finite* if it is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $S$ (00PL (2)). This is the affine notion that the scheme definition [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1) refers to.)

equivalence theorem, not the definition: for [Algebra.FiniteType R S] and q : PrimeSpectrum S, Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber says Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q.asIdeal <-> {q} is open in the subspace comap(algebraMap R S)^{-1}{q.comap} of Spec S; with PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber (Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/ResidueField/Fiber.lean; that subspace is homeomorphic to Spec(p.Fiber S), p.Fiber S = κ(p) ⊗[R] S) this identifies this node's notion with Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q. Since the agreement is a theorem, the node is not a leaf (convention of 2026-10-09); the match is recorded for stage 2
